STEP 3b CLEAN, and the extraction was fully solvable before the rights test stopped it: table_sets.R reports 6 live items attitude_1..attitude_6 with resp {1,2,3,4,5} and n=260/261/260/260/261/261; data/okamura_2018_eol_burnout_attitude.py builds them as {c: f'attitude_{i+1}' for i,c in enumerate(['Q10_1s'..'Q10_6s'])}, i.e. a number-preserving rename of the PLOS S1 .sav columns Q10_1s..Q10_6s, so attitude_N == Q10_Ns with no positional risk. Those six .sav variable labels are '【TC尺度】' topic tags in Japanese -- value / awkwardness / dread / family involvement-physical care / family involvement-holistic involvement / resident-and-family autonomous decision-making -- and they map one-to-one, in order, onto the six sentences of the rights holder's own official short form (fatcod-formb-j-short.pdf, printed in the order items 1, 3, 14, 12, 18, 24 of the full FATCOD-B-J). The .sav value labels also give the administered anchors verbatim (1_全くそうは思わない .. 5_常にそう思う; note the study's own 5th anchor differs from the official form's 5_非常にそう思う). So a data_labels-grade, VERIFIED-grade extraction was available and is not what stopped this table. THE CLAUSE. The Japanese version's rights holder distributes the instrument and its manual from its own page, http://plaza.umin.ac.jp/~fatcod/ (Miyashita M, Univ. of Tokyo / contact miyasita-tky@umin.ac.jp), and the usage manual http://plaza.umin.ac.jp/~fatcod/fatcod_manual.pdf (fetched 2026-09-09, sha256 25ca77d99c1e8ed7ddbfbc344a51e36126e3e658b52fa10e01a74081ae214c8f), section 3 使用許諾について, states verbatim: "本尺度の利用にあたって、特に許可を得る必要はございません。ただし、本尺度の使用にあたり、文章の改変は許可されて下りません。指示文（インストラクション）のみ、研究の状況にあわせて、些細な変更をすることはかまいません。スコアリングのルールを守った上で、自由にお使いいただいて結構です。" ("No particular permission need be obtained to use this scale. However, in using this scale, alteration of the wording is not permitted. Only the instructions may be changed slightly to suit the research situation. You may use it freely provided the scoring rules are observed." -- the 許可されて下りません spelling is the original's own typo for おりません and is quoted as printed.) That is a stated no-derivatives condition on the wording from the wording's rights holder, and no-derivatives is one of the enumerated reserved rights in SKILL.md's test; the HEXACO ruling (2026-09-05, irw#1945) further makes ANY stated use restriction on the only published source of the wording a block, and this page is the only published source of the administered Japanese. IRW's own use would comply -- the transcription would be verbatim -- but per the same test that is not a defence, because hosting hands the wording to downstream users whose alteration IRW cannot condition. ESCALATION FLAG, stated because this sits at the edge of the test: the clause is unusually permissive apart from that one condition (no permission required, no fee, no non-commercial term, no redistribution bar, the questionnaire itself is a free public download from the holder's page), and "do not alter the wording" is at least arguable as an instrument-integrity instruction to administrators rather than a property right reserved against redistribution -- the shape SKILL.md says to escalate rather than decide. Blocked here under 'err on the side of not having things'; a ruling from Ben that an integrity/no-alteration clause is not a reserved right would reopen it immediately, with the extraction already solved above. SECOND, INDEPENDENT ROUTE NOT TAKEN: the English original (Frommelt KH 1991/2003) is a different rights holder one level upstream, and the FATCOD-B-J is a straight back-translation rather than a revision, so shipping the English 6 items as text_source=translated_substitute is not obviously barred by the Japanese page. It was not done, for two reasons: no rights statement for Frommelt's own English could be located to quote either way (secondary sources say the author's consent is sought for adaptations), and substituting the upstream original to route around a block on the administered adaptation is a call for Ben, not for this round. RETRY TEST: NO -- determinate. An unchanged retry right now reaches the same quoted clause on the same page. What would have to change: a ruling from Ben on the integrity-clause question (or on the English-substitute route), or written permission from the FATCOD-B-J rights holder.

note: Not a survey instrument: the 597 `id` units are Polish-language anti-vaccination Facebook posts and the ten `item`s are coding categories the study team applied to each post, so `item_text` is the coding definition rather than a question any respondent read. item_text is transcribed verbatim from PLOS ONE 10.1371/journal.pone.0355341 Table 1 (Definition column), including its inconsistent terminal punctuation -- only the first definition ends in a period, and that is how the paper prints it.
